title: RewardBench 2
evidenceStatus: Full pinned test split: 1,865/1,865 cases, 8,977/8,977 answers; source text/labels/order and official scorer parity independently verified; one scoring pass
summary: The 80.9002% macro score reproduces exactly, and full benchmark coverage is already complete. The Ties mistakes filter hides seven margin-only failures; single-pass close scores and weak baseline comparisons are the main remaining evaluation limitations. A paired case inspector and repeated full comparisons would add more value than another sample.
strengths: Every original case and answer was evaluated; the six subset counts match Ai2's pinned official release.
Independent probe verified all published text, labels, candidate order, attribution and omission hashes against pinned source; all six metrics reproduce from unmodified upstream scoring functions.
255 successful batches contain exactly 8,977 judgments; three unavailable batches recovered, and 279 attempts remain inspectable.
Gold labels and response-model identities are excluded from model inputs, and questions carry isolated candidate text.
Content gates cover every Safety case plus 41 flagged cases; reviewed omissions retain hashes and count toward metrics; ten Bun tests passed.

findings.title: Small ranking gaps lack representative repeatability evidence
findings.evidence: rewardbench2/check-repeats.ts:6,24 repeats one France/Paris fixture; probes/rewardbench2.json finds three identical-question pairs differing by 0.05–0.07, and 106/1,763 ordinary cases with top-two gaps <=0.10, including 33 <=0.02
findings.impact: A single recorded winner does not establish stable preference on close cases or justify small model comparisons; the existing control cannot characterize real-case variability.
findings.fix: Run three full shuffled scheduling passes, preserve all repeats, report winner stability and clustered comparison intervals, and add matched real-question solo/batched controls. Keep official exact-tie scoring unchanged. Add RewardBench tests to the standard app test script and preserve model/run fingerprints.

findings.title: Ties mistake filtering excludes seven failures in the actual metric
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/rewardbench.tsx:23,91 checks ranking only; paired margin fails for ten pairs, but IDs 12,24,27,30,42,44,50 pass both rankings and vanish from that filter
findings.impact: Visitors cannot inspect most paired margin failures through the mistakes view, and reference/tied prompts are disconnected even though the score depends on both.
findings.fix: Navigate 51 linked pairs; render both prompts, matching answer identities, correct-answer spread and rejected-answer gaps. Filter each metric component separately and display the exact composite contribution.

findings.title: Upstream diagnostic metadata is dropped
findings.evidence: rewardbench2/protocol.ts:64 omits additional_metadata; source contains Safety categories for all 450 cases, Factuality method labels for 209 natural and 266 induced cases, and Precise IF instruction IDs
findings.impact: Aggregate category scores hide which source methods and request types cause errors; the viewer cannot explain meaningful benchmark label distinctions.
findings.fix: Preserve metadata for provenance and slice analysis while excluding it from model inputs. Add counts and slice scores plus an annotation/dispute layer that never changes official labels. Carry existing content gates and omission hashes through every new view.

findings.title: Random-only comparison does not show reward-model usefulness
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/rewardbench.tsx:339 shows only 25% uniform selection; shortest-answer baseline earns 52.73% Focus and 37.70% Math from original text; no policy training or independent downstream outcome is recorded
findings.impact: The score establishes static preference recognition, but does not measure gains over simple dataset heuristics, an open reward model, or actual improvement under optimization.
findings.fix: Add deterministic length baselines, a pinned open reward model, and a pre-registered four-dimension Jev ablation on the full split. Create a separate disjoint best-of-N study before attempting reward-driven training; measure quality independently of Jev reward.

findings.title: The full evidence archive blocks initial loading and remains difficult to read
findings.evidence: experience-prototypes/src/main.tsx:47 fetches/parses one 15,844,662-byte JSON; local gzip is 4,669,806 bytes. rewardbench.tsx:284 renders raw Markdown/math; style.css:3623 limits cards to 460px; cases contain up to 38 candidates; raw case disclosure at rewardbench.tsx:319 can reveal labels before voting
findings.impact: Complete evidence exists, but initial loading is unnecessarily large, mathematical answers are harder to compare, and the current interaction cannot produce clean blind votes.
findings.fix: Ship a small index and hashed case/pair chunks plus full archive download. Add expanded safe Markdown/math and raw views, stable deep links, a pair comparison chart, and a separate blind mode that freezes the first vote before exposing gold-bearing diagnostics.

simulation.title: The reward selection desk
simulation.description: Read and choose among anonymous candidates, reveal the dataset and scorer choices, then inspect score gaps and repeat-run winner stability. Ties switches between paired prompts while matching candidate identities stay fixed and score bars animate, exposing the four ranking/margin components. Live BYOK reruns remain exploratory records.
simulation.jevsRole: Score anonymous prompt-and-answer combinations under a frozen rubric; optional comparison protocols score separate quality dimensions.
simulation.codeRole: Preserve candidate identity and pair linkage, compute official metrics and uncertainty, gate sensitive text, render complete safe evidence, manage immutable first votes, and distinguish provider failures from model judgments.
acceptanceCriteria: All 1,763 ordinary cases and 51 linked Ties pairs have stable deep links and complete text or explicit hashed omissions.
All seven margin-only failures are reachable by a component-specific filter and reproduce their exact composite contribution.
Blind mode hides gold, scores, raw records and diagnostic filters until the first vote is fixed.
Duplicate answer positions and differing recorded scores remain visible; charts never invent predictions.
The summary and first case load independently of the full archive; missing chunks show recoverable errors.
Provider outages or cancellation never overwrite completed results or change benchmark metrics.
Every displayed score identifies its run/protocol and is distinguished from calibrated correctness probability.

evaluation.design: Keep pinned official scoring and freeze protocols before comparing. Three fresh full passes with scheduling seeds 42/43/44 require 26,931 candidate judgments, about 765 successful batches at observed packing, before retries. Add 20 preselected real questions repeated ten times in each solo/batched condition, 400 judgments. Use 10,000 stratified paired cluster bootstrap resamples, retaining each Ties pair and repeated source-prompt cluster; report run variation separately. Develop rubric weights and abstention thresholds on disjoint data. A four-dimension ablation requires 35,908 judgments per full pass. A separate downstream study can use 200 disjoint tasks, eight candidates and three generation seeds, 4,800 candidate judgments per scorer, with verifier or blinded human outcomes.
baselines: Uniform random selection, 25% for ordinary categories
Shortest and longest original answers with split credit for equal length
Pinned open reward model using its documented scoring contract
Pre-registered correctness/instruction/relevance/appropriateness Jev scores, weights fixed on separate development data
For downstream selection: generator first answer, random selection and independent verifier/human outcome
metrics: Official six-category macro and all subset scores
Paired 95% cluster-bootstrap differences and run-to-run variation
Winner flip rate, exact ties and close score gaps
Ties reference/tied accuracy, margin tests and smooth bonus
Safety and source-method slice scores with counts
Risk versus coverage and held-out calibration for escalation policies
Downstream independently measured quality versus Jev reward

coverage.current: 1,865/1,865 unique test cases and 8,977/8,977 candidate answers. Three prompts and six answers are omitted from public display only; all remain scored.
coverage.full: The official pinned release has one 1,865-case test split: Focus 495, Factuality 475, Math 183, Safety 450, Precise IF 160, Ties 102 as 51 linked pairs.
coverage.feasibility: Already complete. One further pass needs 8,977 candidate judgments, approximately 255 successful batches with current packing. Two additional passes need 17,954 judgments; three fresh passes need 26,931. No generation calls or new dataset download are required. Provider scheduling/retry handling is the remaining operational concern; no case-size blocker was found. Recorded cost values are zero and cannot alone establish actual billing.
